channel.title: Above the Ruin
channel.description: Recent content on Above the Ruin

item.title: Refactoring for Saving
item.description:
Up until now, I’ve been having fun creating systems. However, when it came to wiring them up, I was a bit cavalier with how that was done. I did try to separate concerns as much as possible, having controllers to do the logic while renderers would listen to events that they emitted.

However, if we take the PlayerController as an example, it had a lot of references on it for UI. Things like the dialogue wrapper, conversation box etc. For this vertical slice, it wasn’t too bad. However, I’m at the stage now where I need to move the player to a new scene.

item.title: Producer Levels
item.description:
I’ve added a couple of “passive producers” to Above the Ruin.

Their purspose is to produce an item after n hours. For example, the water collector will produce water every 8 hours*. The bee house will produce honey every 16 hours*.

*all timings to be confirmed

But how do you tell the player that the item is ready to be collected? Some games show a tool tip above the producer to alert you. While this was an option, I wanted to see if I could have the producer visually tell the player that it’s ready.

item.title: Item Definitions
item.description: With a lot of items in Above the Ruin, it’s important that I get them right. They should be easy to create and easy to extend. Items can range from something like carrots, to water collectors equipped with a tarp funnel. Each one can have several different properties like being able to consume them or place them in the world and finding a way nice way to do this was tricky.

item.title: Removing Actions from Dialogue
item.description: The dialogue system has gotten a bit too complex and is doing too much. When I wrote the system, which was the first one I wrote, I envisioned dialogue with actions. Those actions could trigger before text is rendered or when the interact button was pressed. Actions would be ran sequentially. For example in the JSON below, the NPC would move down 1 tile, then up 1 tile. There was also an action to move the camera, which followed the same schema.

item.title: The Tileset So Far
item.description:
After playing around with pixel art for a few days, I’m pleased to share what I have so far. I decided to put it all together in a way that a player might place their buildings.

There’s room for improvement, but it’s starting to look like an actual game now.

item.title: Pixel Art is Hard (Part Deux)
item.description:
Following on from Pixel Art is Hard, I decided to spend some more time creating props for Above the Ruin.

One of the important aspects of the game will be water. There will be a few ways of obtaining it, from basic buckets to water collection systems. For now, I spent some time creating a tank, which will collect a small amount of water passively. This can be upgraded with a tarp to funnel more water in to the tank, increasing the generation.

item.title: Dialogue - What do I say?
item.description:
The first system I designed when I started Above the Ruin was the dialogue system. I wanted something that would make it easy to write dialogue, but also easy to extend for potential modders.

The first part was how to load in the dialogue. I went with JSON files as this is easier to manage, structured and can be extended.

{
  "dialog": {
    "16_spring": {
      "text": "So, {playerName}...",
      "nextNode": "nextOne"
    },
    "nextOne": {
      "portrait": "angry",
      "actions": [{
        "type": "moveNPC",
        "targetRelativePosition": {
          "y": -1
        }
      }],
      "text": "It's day {dayNumber} of {season}. Are you sure you want to go down in to the tower?",
      "choices": [{
        "text": "Yes",
        "nextNode": "nextOne_yes"
      }, {
        "text": "No",
        "nextNode": "nextOne_no"
      }]
    },
    ...

Each object in the JSON represents a line of dialogue, with several options depending on the NPC and the conversation.

item.title: Pixel Art is Hard
item.description:
I’m at the stage now where I have a few systems in place, but I’m tired of staring at basic shapes and a grey-boxed world.

I am a backend engineer, so stuff like art doesn’t come naturally to me. However, I’ve always admired pixel art, having grown up in the age of Mario on the Snes. I was also inspired by Eric Barone, the creator of Stardew Valley. He managed to do all of the pixel art himself.

item.title: About "Above the Ruin"
item.description:
Above the Ruin is a cozy game, such as Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon. However, I’ve decided to go with darker tones and themes.

The game is set in a post-apocalyptic setting, where survivors live on the rooftops of skyscrapers.

The rooftop is your home. Here, you’ll be able to do all the cozy things, such as farming, tending to your animals, and so on.

If you fancy leaving the safety of the rooftops, you can choose to descend through the tower. Here, you’ll be able to fight off enemies, explore abandoned homes and offices and find loot to improve life on the surface.

item.title: Welcome
item.description:
This blog will serve as updates for the game, from technical challenges, artistic ones, or just random thoughts throughout my journey.

Making a game has always been a dream of mine. I got in to the Web Software Engineering industry about 15 years ago, but I’ve always wished I got in to game development early on.

Above the Ruin is a passion project that I’m working on in my spare time. If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out at hello@abovetheruin.com.
